title: Measure 40 Worm Feeding with Bioluminescent Bacteria
author: Serena Ding
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5hsg36e
materials: Initialise the IVIS system via the LivingImage software.

Set up imaging parameters within the LivingImage software interface. Set stage temperature to 20 °C , designate auto-saving directory for acquired images, and set up acquisition sequence parameters. Bioluminescence acquisition parameters: subject height: 0.5 cm; field of view: C; expososure: 1 second; frame interval: 6 minutes; excitation: block; emission: open; luminescence binning: 4; photograph binning: 4; luminescence F/stop: 1; photograph F/stop: 1; batch sequence: true; sequence 1 length: 99; sequence 2 length: 35. These imaging parameters have been determined in advance for the experiment and are saved as a .xsq configuration file, which can be loaded into the imaging software.

steps.title: Prepare Bioluminescent Bacteria Stock
steps.instruction: Streak out bioluminescent bacteria frozen stock onto an LB plate containing 50 μg/mL ampicillin and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Note: A streaked plate can be re-used within 1 month if single colonies are available; otherwise, re-streak onto a new LB/ampicillin plate.

steps.title: Prepare Overnight Bacteria Culture
steps.instruction: At ~5pm on Day -1, prepare a bacteria culture in a 300 mL volumetric flask.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 mL LB broth and 100 μL ampicillin stock solution (50mg/mL) to the flask.
Inoculate with a single colony of bioluminescent bacteria from the streaked plate.
Incubate at 37 °C shaking at 220 rpm overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Bacteria for Seeding
steps.instruction: At ~10am on Day 0, remove the overnight culture from the shaking incubator and leave it at room temperature on the bench until use.

substeps.instruction: Do not store the culture at 4 °C as this will abolish the signal.

steps.title: Prepare Imaging Plates
steps.instruction: Warm the imaging plates (35 mm Petri dish containing 3.5 mL low peptone agar) by taking them out of the 4 °C cold room and incubating at room temperature for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Seed Bacteria onto Plates
steps.instruction: Seed the bioluminescent bacteria onto the imaging plates and dry them.

substeps.instruction: Swirl the flask containing the overnight culture to resuspend cells.
Measure the optical density of the bacteria culture with a spectrophotometer for the record.
Seed 20 μL of the bacteria culture onto the center of each 35 mm imaging plate.
Dry the plates in a laminar flow hood (setting II) for 30 minutes.
Retrieve plates from the flow hood and label them with the sample name.

steps.title: Prepare Synchronized Adult Worms
steps.instruction: Bleach synchronize animals from three 60mm plates containing gravid hermaphrodites.

substeps.instruction: Leave on a rotator at 20 °C until use.
Re-feed worms onto 60mm plates using a glass pipette and incubate at 20 °C.
Monitor plates to ensure worms do not run out of food.

steps.title: Harvest and Wash Worms
steps.instruction: Harvest synchronized adult worms and remove contaminating bacteria.

substeps.instruction: Harvest worms using 2 mL of M9 buffer and transfer into a 15 mL tube.
Wash worms twice with M9 buffer by topping up the tube with M9, spinning at 1500 rpm/210 rcf (ascending 9, descending 7), and aspiring the supernatant.
Leave the loose worm pellet after the final wash.

steps.title: Transfer Worms to Imaging Plates
steps.instruction: Transfer exactly 40 worms to each imaging plate using a glass pipette with a medicine dropper bulb.

substeps.instruction: Use a manual click counter to count 40 worms per plate.
Keep the droplet small to ensure it is absorbed into the media within a couple of minutes.
If necessary, use a P20 pipette containing a few microliters of M9 to carefully suck out excess worms and recount.
Place the lid back onto the imaging plate.

steps.title: Prepare Samples for IVIS Imaging
steps.instruction: Transport and prepare the plates for the IVIS imaging system.

substeps.instruction: Place samples inside a cardboard box, then inside a styrofoam box, and carry carefully to the IVIS system.
Ensure the liquid drop has been completely absorbed into the media.
Vortex imaging samples for 10s on the lowest setting of a vortex mixer to disperse aggregates and randomize worm positions.

steps.title: Acquire IVIS Images
steps.instruction: Perform image acquisition using the IVIS system.

substeps.instruction: Place imaging samples inside the IVIS chamber within the laser grid guidelines and close the door.
Start acquisition via the software exactly 1 min after the vortex start.

steps.title: Analyze Imaging Data
steps.instruction: Process the acquired image sequence using LivingImage software.

substeps.instruction: Measure radiance (photons/s) for a defined region of interest across the acquisition sequence.
Export the signal as a tab-delimited text file for downstream analysis.
